scope: Fact-check of corrosion, stainless steels, cast irons, aluminum alloys, casting and solidification cards in lecture/self-assessment modules plus visible Corrosion & SS and Al & Casting topic cards matching the scope.
summary: No critical, major or minor factual issues found in the scoped cards. Correct-answer letters matched the course evidence, and the explanations align with the corrosion/stainless, cast iron, aluminum alloy, and casting/solidification sources reviewed.

uncertainties.note: The card's warning that precipitation-hardened aluminium alloys may suffer stress-corrosion cracking near precipitate-free zones is metallurgically plausible and consistent with the Lecture 14 summary showing lower corrosion resistance for high-strength age-hardened families, but the extracted/visible course slide text did not explicitly name precipitate-free zones. Keep if lecture discussion covered PFZs; otherwise simplify to the course-supported statement that age hardening/high-strength Al families can trade strength against corrosion resistance.

The card's note that 7xxx precipitation microstructures can be sensitive to stress-corrosion cracking, especially near grain-boundary precipitate-free zones, is plausible but more detailed than the directly visible Lecture 14 slide/notes wording. The course sources clearly support 7xxx as high-strength, age-hardened, aircraft-use and not highly weldable; PFZ-specific wording should be confirmed against instructor oral notes if strict source minimalism is required.
